title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: In K-linked Preyssler frameworks, occluded PEG can contribute to proton transport through polymer segmental motion, whereas a PAA-containing analogue is the humidity-stable member and reaches higher proton conductivity.
explanation: W7a–c are built from [Na(H2O)P5W30O110]14− linked by K+, with PEG400, PEG1000, or PAA5000 in the crystallization. Relatively high activation energies for W7a and W7b are interpreted as PEG segmental motion assisting proton conduction, but both have limited stability at high relative humidity. W7c remains stable and reaches 1.7×10−3 S cm−1 at 338 K and 75% RH.
scope: Polyoxotungstate frameworks W7a–c based on the Preyssler anion with PEG or polyallylamine guests.
conditions: Hydrothermal assembly of the Preyssler salt with KNO3 and the polymer; proton conductivity from impedance spectra and Arrhenius plots.
caveats: The segmental-motion explanation is an inference from activation energies. Conductivity and stability differences are specific to these three polymer-containing phases.
